newsitem.title: USA: Foundation says will have net loss in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Foundation says will have net loss in Q2.

text.p: Foundation Health Systems Inc said Friday it will record a net loss for the second quarter after accounting for the effect of non-recurring charges.
Before the effect of the charges, the company said it expects earnings to be in the range of $0.49 to $0.51 per share.
The company said it plans to take about $348.4 million in pre-tax merger, restructuring and other one-time charges in its second quarter.
These charges are higher than original estimates.
In addition, it said it will take a $57.5 million pre-tax charge related to the reinsurance of its Gem Insurance Co operations.
The merger-related charges cover costs associated with the April 1 merger involving Foundation Health Corp and Health Systems International Inc, which created Foundation Health Systems.
In the joint merger proxy, the companies had estimated these charges would fall between $175 million and $225 million.
The charges cover merger-related and other non-recurring costs including severance and employee benefit payments, real estate lease buyouts and legal and investment banking costs.
The company said it will include these charges as part of its second quarter earnings announcement, scheduled for August 12.

"We have had the opportunity to comprehensively review the impact of the merger on the company's ongoing operations," said chairman and chief executive Malik Hasan. "We determined that several categories of these charges needed to be expanded to reflect both the realities of the businesses and our long-term goals."
